what is the fastest land animal?: The cheetah can sprint up to about 100-120 km/h (60-75 mph) in short bursts. It runs down prey in less than a minute before tiring.
what is grumpy cat's real name?: Grumpy Cat, whose real name was Tardar Sauce, became an internet star in 2012 for her permanently frowning face, caused by feline dwarfism and an underbite. She died in 2019.
snakes and lizards are known to flick th: Snakes and lizards flick their tongues to pick up scent particles from the air and ground. The tongue delivers them to the Jacobson's organ in the roof of the mouth.
what colour is the female blackbird?: The female blackbird is brown, with a streaked chest, while the male is glossy black with a yellow-orange bill. The difference helps females stay camouflaged on the nest.
wombats are native to which country?: Wombats are marsupials native to Australia, including Tasmania. They have backward-facing pouches and make cube-shaped droppings.
of the giant clam, giant crab and giant: The giant clam (Tridacna gigas) can have a shell over a meter (4 feet) across, weighing hundreds of pounds. It is the largest living bivalve mollusc.
all of these animals have large ears (re: Polar bears have small, rounded ears, which reduce heat loss in the Arctic. Animals in hot places, such as fennec foxes and jackrabbits, have large ears to release heat.
cobras are venomous snakes of family ela: King cobras and true cobras live in Asia and Africa, in the family Elapidae. The family also includes mambas, coral snakes and sea snakes.
name the rarest and most endangered of a: The red wolf (Canis rufus) of the southeastern US is one of the world's most endangered canids. Only about 20 live in the wild, in North Carolina.
jack jumper ants, yellowish-orange carni: Jack jumper ants (Myrmecia pilosula) are found only in Australia, mostly in Tasmania and southern regions. Their sting can cause severe allergic reactions in some people.
which word refers to the sound peacocks: Peacocks make a loud, piercing call that is often described as a scream or a "may-awe". The males also fan out their tails to attract peahens.
"French Twist" is a hairstyle, not a cat breed. Real breeds include the Siamese, Maine Coon and Persian.
which of the following is not a type of: "Glass spider" isn't a recognized spider type. Real spiders include the orb weaver, wolf spider and jumping spider (David Bowie had a "Glass Spider" tour).
all but one of the following are true ty: The moon bear is another name for the Asiatic black bear, which is a real bear with a crescent-shaped white patch on its chest. The eight bear species include polar, brown, black, sun, sloth, spectacled and giant panda.
which of these is not an actual breed of: Real sheep breeds include Merino, Suffolk and Dorset. The "Dakota" is not a standard breed, although there are Dakota-region sheep operations.
what is the average lifespan of a lion l: A wild lion lives about 10-14 years, with males often dying earlier due to fights. In captivity, lions can reach 20 years.
if a cat pushes its face against your he: When a cat bumps its head against you, it's called head bunting. It shows affection and trust, and it also leaves scent from glands on the cat's face.
which statement about elephants is untru: Elephants do have excellent memories. They remember water sources, routes and other elephants for decades, and matriarchs lead herds with this knowledge.
what type of animal is a lamprey?: Lampreys are jawless fish with a round, sucker-like mouth. Some species attach to other fish and feed on their blood.
chihuahuas are the only dogs to be born: Chihuahuas are born with a soft spot (molera) in the skull, as human babies are, which may remain open into adulthood. They are the smallest dog breed.
what is the average lifespan of chihuahu: Chihuahuas typically live 12-20 years, among the longest of any dog breed. Smaller dogs tend to outlive larger breeds.
what does the word \"hippopotamus\" mean: "Hippopotamus" comes from Greek words meaning "river horse". Hippos are in fact more closely related to whales than horses.
also called sea biscuit, this animal liv: A sand dollar is a flat, disc-shaped sea urchin that lives partially buried in sandy seafloors. The white "dollars" found on beaches are their skeletons, called tests.
chameleons are lizards that can change t: "Chameleon" comes from the Greek "chamai leon", meaning "ground lion" or "earth lion". The lizards change color for communication and temperature control, not just camouflage.
this sharks white belly and grey back ma: The great white shark is dark on top and white below, a pattern called countershading. From above it blends with the deep water, and from below it blends with the bright surface.
which of these sharks has a flat body li: The angel shark has a flattened body and wide pectoral fins that look like a ray. It lies buried in the sand and ambushes fish.
what is the typical lifespan of the beag: Beagles typically live 12-15 years. They are scent hounds with a strong nose, bred for hunting rabbits.
what type of coat do beagles have?: Beagles have a short to medium-length, dense coat. It sheds regularly and comes in tricolor, lemon and other patterns.
how long can a goldfish live in optimal: Goldfish can live 20 years or more in good conditions, and the record is over 40. In small bowls, they usually die much sooner.
what color are wild goldfish?: Wild goldfish (relatives of carp) are olive-green or brownish. Orange and gold colors came from selective breeding in China.
the coyote lives in north america and al: The coyote (Canis latrans) is also called the prairie wolf or brush wolf. It's native to North America and has expanded into cities.
what type of animal is the cottonmouth?: The cottonmouth (water moccasin) is a venomous pit viper of the southeastern US. It gets its name from the white inside of its mouth when threatened.
which of these coat colors is not found: Red foxes come in several color forms, such as red, silver (black) and cross. The black and silver morph is a rarer variant of the same species.
which of the following color of egg is i: Chicken eggs can be white, brown, blue or green, depending on the breed, but not black. Shell color is determined by the hen's genetics.
what is the average lifespan of a lion i: Wild lions live about 10-14 years, though some live longer. Females in a pride tend to live longer than males.
what does the word penguin mean?: The word "penguin" may come from the Welsh "pen gwyn" (white head) or from Latin "pinguis", meaning fat. Its exact origin is debated.
which of these animals is not a natural: Polar bears and penguins live at opposite ends of the Earth, so polar bears don't hunt them. Penguin predators include leopard seals, orcas, skuas and sharks.
what color is a polar bears skin?: A polar bear's skin is black, which absorbs heat, and its hairs are transparent hollow tubes that look white. This helps it stay warm.
what is the estimated average lifespan o: Large crocodiles can live 70 years or more, and some may reach a century. Smaller species typically live 30-50 years.
on which of these continents can you fin: Saltwater crocodiles live in northern Australia, Southeast Asia and eastern India. They're the largest living reptile, reaching 6 m (20 ft).
why does a cat bury his/ her waste?: Cats bury their waste partly to hide their scent from predators and rivals. It is an instinct from wild ancestors.
why do cats like to sleep in the sun?: Cats sleep in the sun to keep warm, because their body temperature drops during sleep. Their ideal ambient temperature is higher than ours.
approximately how tall is a grizzly bear: Grizzly bears can stand 2.4 m (8 ft) tall on their hind legs, and weigh up to 360 kg (800 lb) or more. They stand to see and smell better.
in which country is the grizzly bear lis: Grizzly bears are listed as threatened in the lower 48 states of the US under the Endangered Species Act. Alaska and Canada have larger populations.
although the grizzly bear is on the flag: The California grizzly bear is on the state flag, and the last one in the state was killed in 1922. The grizzly is the state animal.
the does \"cheetah\" mean translated fro: "Cheetah" comes from the Hindi "chita", from Sanskrit "chitraka", meaning "spotted one". It's the fastest land animal.
which of these is not a sound made by ch: Cheetahs can't roar. They chirp, purr, growl and hiss, because their larynx structure differs from lions and tigers.
what is the typical lifespan of the chee: Wild cheetahs live about 10-12 years, while captive cheetahs can live up to 20 years. They are vulnerable to extinction.
what is the smallest frog?: The Brazilian gold frog (Brachycephalus didactylus) is about 1 cm long and among the smallest vertebrates. The tiny frog lives in leaf litter in Brazil's Atlantic forest.
this type of ant causes a lot of allergi: Fire ants have a painful, burning sting and cause many allergic reactions in the southern US. They were accidentally imported from South America in the 1930s.
this type of ant is considered the most: The jack jumper ant has a sting that is dangerous to allergic people in Australia. Some scientists rank harvester ants as having more toxic venom.
about how long have ants been around on: Ants evolved during the Cretaceous period, well over 100 million years ago. Fossil ants date back as far as 100-140 million years.
why were thylacines called tigers?: Thylacines (Tasmanian tigers) had dark stripes across their backs, giving them a tiger-like look. The last known one died in captivity in 1936.
what does the malaysian word pangolin me: "Pangolin" comes from the Malay "pengguling", meaning "one who rolls up". When threatened, it curls into a ball.
which of these statements concerning the: Pangolins defend themselves by curling into a ball with their scales outward, not by outrunning predators. They are slow-moving and heavily trafficked.
Running away from a big cat can trigger its chase instinct. Experts say to stay calm, face the cat, make yourself look large and back away slowly.
although only a small percent of scorpio: Scorpions are mostly nocturnal, hiding during the day under rocks. They glow under ultraviolet light.
which of the following statements about: Most snakes avoid humans and bite only when threatened or stepped on. Snakes don't normally attack people on sight.
in which of these african environments a: Hyenas live in savannas, grasslands, forests and mountains, and even semi-deserts such as the Namib. They are found throughout much of Africa.
which of these is not a species of hyena: There are four living hyena species: the spotted, striped, brown and aardwolf. There is no "golden" hyena, though the golden jackal exists.
what is a group of hyenas called?: A group of hyenas is called a clan. Spotted hyena clans are led by females.
which of these european countries is not: Wild reindeer (caribou) live in the northern parts of Europe, such as Norway, Finland and Russia, but not Switzerland. They were in the Alps during the last Ice Age.
how long is the average lifespan of an e: Elephants live about 60-70 years in the wild. Their lifespan is similar to humans.
through what body part can an elephant n: Elephants hear through their large ears, and can also detect low-frequency vibrations through their feet and trunk. They communicate through infrasound.
the echidnas diet consists mainly of thi: Echidnas (spiny anteaters) eat mostly ants, termites and other insects, which they catch with a long sticky tongue. They are egg-laying mammals.
where does the kookaburra, a common aust: "Kookaburra" comes from Wiradjuri, an Aboriginal language (guuguubarra), imitating the bird's laughing call. It's the largest kingfisher.
how many cubs are usually in a tigers li: A tigress usually gives birth to two to four cubs. The cubs stay with their mother for about two years.
which country does the clydesdale horse: The Clydesdale horse originated in Clydesdale, Lanarkshire, in Scotland, in the 1700s. It's known for its feathered feet.
what class of horse breed does the clyde: Clydesdales are draft horses, bred for farm work and heavy hauling. The Budweiser Clydesdales are well-known.
what common name does the dog breed new: The New Guinea Highland Dog is also called the "singer" for its distinctive howl. It's closely related to the New Guinea singing dog.
in what european country did the rough c: The Rough Collie originated in Scotland, as a herding dog. It's best known as Lassie.
what is the definition of the term hyper: A hypercarnivore gets over 70% of its diet from meat. Examples include lions, wolves and orcas.
whiteflies generally feed on what?: Whiteflies are tiny insects that feed on the sap of plant leaves, usually on the undersides. They can damage crops and spread plant viruses.
in what country did the american akita d: The Akita originated in Japan, and the American Akita was developed later in the US. Hachiko is the famous Akita dog.
the nutria is native to which continent?: The nutria (coypu) is a rodent native to South America, introduced elsewhere for fur. It's now an invasive species in North America and Europe.
which of the following is a characterist: Nutria have large orange incisors, with a coating of iron. They also have webbed hind feet.
what do farmers raise nutrias for?: Nutria were raised for fur on fur farms, and escapes created wild populations. Their fur is called "river mink".
what is the yorkshire terriers average l: Yorkshire Terriers typically live 11-15 years. They were bred in the 1800s to catch rats in textile mills.
the northern short-tailed shrew is a sma: The northern short-tailed shrew has venomous saliva, and lives in the northeastern US and southeastern Canada. It uses it to subdue prey such as mice.
what is a group of jellyfish called?: A group of jellyfish is called a bloom, smack or swarm. Blooms can number in the thousands.
what is the largest fish in existence?: The whale shark is the largest fish, reaching 12 m (40 ft) or more. It's a filter feeder and harmless to people.
what is the largest living terrestrial o: The African bush elephant is the largest living land animal. The largest organism by area is a honey fungus (Armillaria) in Oregon, or by mass, the aspen grove called Pando.
where are vampire bats mostly found?: Vampire bats live in Mexico, Central America and South America. They feed on blood from livestock and wild animals.
what is the largest wolf species on the: The gray wolf (Canis lupus) is the largest wild canid. Wolves in northern regions, such as Alaska and Canada, grow largest.
wolf pups are usually born with irises o: Wolf pups are born with blue eyes, which turn amber or yellow at around eight weeks old. They are born deaf and blind.
to what continent is the unique maned wo: The maned wolf lives in South America, in grasslands of Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Bolivia. It is the largest canid there and has long legs.
what kind of animal is the spotted wobbe: The spotted wobbegong is a carpet shark that lives on the seabed off eastern Australia. It uses its camouflage to ambush prey.
what is the common name of the quoll, a: Quolls are carnivorous marsupials of Australia and New Guinea, sometimes called "native cats". They have spotted fur.
which of these areas is the black salama: The black salamander (Aneides flavipunctatus) lives in northern California and southern Oregon. It's a lungless salamander.
how did the black mamba snake get its na: The black mamba is named for the inside of its mouth, which is black, and displayed when threatened. Its skin is olive-gray to brown.
in nature, chinchillas can be found in o: Wild chinchillas are gray. Selective breeding for the fur trade has produced many colors.
which of the following should be avoided: Fresh vegetables and fruits can cause digestive upset (bloating, diarrhea) in chinchillas. Their diet should consist mainly of hay and pellets.
which of these physiological features do: Chinchillas can't sweat and overheat easily. They're best kept below 25 °C (77 °F).
which breed group does the chinese crest: The Chinese Crested belongs to the Toy group. It comes in hairless and powderpuff varieties.
what notable feature does the fennec fox: The fennec fox has enormous ears, which help it hear prey underground and shed heat in the Sahara. It's the smallest fox.
to which of these geographical areas are: Hummingbirds are native only to the Americas, from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego. There are more than 300 species.
how did the smallest bird in the world,: The bee hummingbird is named because of its size, about 5-6 cm (2 in), no bigger than a large bee. It lives in Cuba.
what type of mammal is the culpeo?: The culpeo is a South American fox, also called the Andean fox. It's the second largest canid there.
which of the following is a characterist: Tiger sharks give birth to live young (ovoviviparous), with litters of 10-80 pups. They're named for stripes on their sides when young.
what does the latin word omnivore stand: "Omnivore" comes from Latin "omnis" (all) and "vorare" (to devour). Humans, bears and pigs are omnivores.
what is the main food source for the slo: Sloths eat mostly leaves, buds and twigs. They have a slow metabolism, so they digest food slowly.
what is the prevailing color of the fur: Tasmanian devils have black fur, with a white patch on the chest. They have a powerful bite.
in what part of their body do tasmanian: Tasmanian devils store fat in their tails. A thick tail means a healthy devil.
at what time of the day are tasmanian de: Tasmanian devils are mostly nocturnal. They scavenge at night.
in what geographical region can you find: The paradise tree snake is found in Southeast Asia. It glides from tree to tree by flattening its body.
what body part of the giraffe can indica: Giraffes' horns (ossicones) differ by sex: males have bald tops from sparring, and females have tufts of hair. Males use their necks in fights.
the family \"delphinidae\" include which: Delphinidae is the family of oceanic dolphins, including bottlenose dolphins and orcas. Porpoises belong to a different family.
the microraptor, the smallest known non-: Microraptor lived in China in the early Cretaceous, and had four wings. It was about the size of a crow.
what type of animal is the smallest vert: The smallest known vertebrate is a frog, Paedophryne amauensis, at 7.7 mm, though small fish such as Paedocypris are also tiny. Both live in Southeast Asia/Papua New Guinea.
the smallest turtle in the world, the sp: The speckled padloper tortoise is the smallest tortoise in the world, native to South Africa and Namibia. It's only about 8-10 cm long.
what color is the crest on the head of t: The southern rockhopper penguin has a yellow crest above its red eyes. It breeds on sub-Antarctic islands.
most penguin species are piscivorous, me: "Piscivorous" means fish-eating. Most penguins eat fish, krill and squid.
what is the special talent of the pengui: Mumble, the main penguin in Happy Feet (2006), can't sing but is a great tap dancer. The dance steps were motion-captured from Savion Glover.
what is the weight range of normal matur: Adult platypuses weigh 0.7-2.4 kg (1.5-5 lb). Males are larger and have a venomous spur.
to what geographic area is the ostrich n: Ostriches are native to Africa. They are the largest living bird.
the feathers of adult male ostriches are: Adult male ostriches have mostly black plumage with white wing and tail feathers. Females are brown-gray.
how many toes do ostriches have?: Ostriches have only two toes on each foot, unlike other birds. This helps them run fast.
which of these statements is true about: Jackson's chameleon gives birth to live young, 8-30 at a time. Males have three horns.
how many times per year is a healthy fem: Guinea pigs can have up to five litters a year. Each litter has two to four pups.
what geographic area did the guinea pig: Guinea pigs originated in the Andes of South America. They were domesticated for food over 3,000 years ago.
what type of food does the guinea pig na: Guinea pigs eat grass and hay. They also need vitamin C in their diet.
in this 2009 walt disney action comedy m: G-Force (2009) is a Disney film about guinea pigs who are secret agents. It combined live action and CGI.
to what continent are raccoons native?: Raccoons are native to North America. They've also been introduced to Europe and Japan.
raccoons are omnivorous animals but they: Raccoons are omnivorous and eat fruits, nuts, insects and small animals. They're opportunistic feeders.
what is the most important sense for rac: Raccoons have a very sensitive sense of touch in their front paws. They "wash" food to feel it.
why is it not recommended to be keep rac: Raccoons aren't recommended as pets, as they can be aggressive, destructive and carry diseases. It's also illegal in many places.
what have raccoons been mostly hunted fo: Raccoons have been hunted mostly for their fur. Their meat has also been eaten.
how did the glass lizard, also known as: Glass lizards (glass snakes) are legless lizards whose tails break off easily when caught. The tail then regrows.
what feature of the turtle species dermo: The leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) has no hard shell, but a leathery skin over bone. It's the largest sea turtle.
in what geographical area is the rock mo: The rock monitor lizard is found in sub-Saharan Africa. "Legavaan" is the Afrikaans name.
where is the natural habitat of sloths?: Sloths live in the rainforests of Central and South America. They spend almost all their time in trees.
sloths have this number of toes and fing: Two-toed sloths have two fingers and three toes, and three-toed sloths have three on both. All have long claws.
how many hours of sleep do sloths normal: Wild sloths sleep only about 9-10 hours a day, not 15-20 as in captivity. They are active at night.
how many babies do female sloths give bi: Sloths give birth to a single baby after a six-month pregnancy (three-toed) or longer (two-toed). The baby clings to its mother.
what term is used to refer to the young: A baby kangaroo is called a joey. It lives in its mother's pouch for months.
male western grey kangaroos were nicknam: Male Western Grey Kangaroos are nicknamed "stinkers" because of their curry-like smell. Both sexes have a distinct musk.
what is the meaning of the word kangaroo: A popular legend says "kangaroo" means "I don't understand", but this is a myth. The word is from the Guugu Yimithirr language (gangurru), meaning a grey kangaroo.
what is the average lifespan of a mudpup: Mudpuppies can live for 11 years or more in the wild and longer in captivity. They are fully aquatic salamanders.
in which of the following states will yo: Mudpuppies live in eastern and central North America, from Canada to the southern US. They're found in Texas in the eastern half of the state, but not everywhere.
how long is the average mudpuppy?: Mudpuppies are about 20-33 cm (8-13 in) long, with some reaching 40 cm. They have red feathery gills.
how many babies does the female wombat g: Wombats typically give birth to a single joey, which spends months in the pouch. The pouch faces backward to keep out dirt.
what should a person do to escape the at: Wombats can be aggressive and powerful, and could injure people. Climbing a tree is a way to escape.
which continent does the turtle-dove mig: European turtle-doves migrate to sub-Saharan Africa for the winter. Their numbers have declined sharply.
which of the following statements is tru: Turtle-doves are seen as a symbol of love and fidelity, as in "The Twelve Days of Christmas". They mate for life.
what is the expected lifespan of a turtl: Turtle-doves live about 3-8 years in the wild, and can live up to 20 years in captivity.
what is the incubation period for turtle: Turtle-dove eggs hatch after about 13-14 days. Both parents incubate them.
what are the main colors of turtle-doves: European turtle-doves are mainly brown and gray, with striped patches on the neck. They are small doves.
what is the greatest depth the shell of: A nautilus shell can withstand pressure down to about 800 m (2,600 ft) before imploding. They live in deep water.
what is the average lifespan of a nautil: Nautiluses can live around 20 years, much longer than other cephalopods. They are "living fossils".
what is the color of the legs, bill and: The green magpie has a red bill and red legs, and bright green plumage. It lives in the forests of Southeast Asia.
to what country is the rhinoderma rufum,: Rhinoderma rufum, the Chile Darwin's frog, is endemic to Chile. The male carries tadpoles in his vocal sac.
what interesting characteristic do all a: Caecilians are legless, limbless amphibians that look like worms or snakes. They live underground in tropical areas.
what does the diet of the eastern tiger: The eastern tiger salamander eats insects, worms and small animals. It's one of the largest land salamanders.
where does the female suriname toad keep: The female Suriname toad carries her eggs embedded in the skin of her back until they develop into toadlets. The young emerge fully formed.
in what places does the nocturnal aye-ay: The aye-aye sleeps by day in nests built in trees. It's nocturnal and lives in Madagascar.
what is the aye-aye traditionally associ: In Malagasy legends, the aye-aye is an omen of death, and some people kill it on sight. That superstition is a big threat to the species.
to what geographic area is the koala end: Koalas live only in eastern Australia, in eucalyptus forests. They aren't bears; they are marsupials.
when anxious, the koala produces a loud: When distressed, koalas make loud sounds like a screaming human baby. Males also make deep bellows.
what is the literal meaning of the word: "Giraffe" comes from the Arabic "zarafa", and its exact meaning is debated, with suggestions such as "fast-walker" or "lovely one". Giraffes are the tallest land animals.
the horns of which giraffes are very oft: Male giraffes often have bald ossicones, because they use their heads in "necking" fights. Females' horns have tufts of hair.
of all mammals, giraffes require the lea: Giraffes sleep very little, often only 30 minutes to two hours a day in short naps. They sleep standing or lying with their neck curled back.
what does the name of the zebra literall: The word "zebra" may come from a Portuguese word for wild ass. Zebras are in the horse family.
what animal is the number one predator o: Lions are the main predator of zebras, though hyenas, wild dogs and crocodiles also hunt them. Zebra stripes may help confuse predators.
what is the common length of a full grow: A male Komodo dragon is about 2.5 m (8-9 ft) long on average. It's the largest living lizard.
how heavy was the largest verified wild: The largest verified wild Komodo dragon weighed about 166 kg (365 lb). Captive ones can be heavier.
what is the top speed that a komodo drag: A Komodo dragon can run up to about 20 km/h (13 mph) in short bursts. It's usually an ambush hunter.
how fast can a black bear run?: A black bear can run about 48 km/h (30 mph), faster than any human. It can also climb trees and swim.
which of the following is not a nickname: Polar bears are known as "ice bears", "white bears" or "sea bears" (Ursus maritimus means "maritime bear"). "Great bear" is the meaning of "Ursa Major" instead.
how many years does a mother grizzly sta: Grizzly cubs stay with their mother for about two to three years, learning to hunt and find food. Females then mate again.
what of these members of the bear family: The polar bear is the largest bear and the largest land carnivore. Males weigh 350-700 kg (770-1,540 lb).
where do orphaned grizzly cubs grinder a: Grinder and Coola are orphaned grizzly bears who live at Grouse Mountain near Vancouver, British Columbia. They became famous after their rescue.
how fast can a domestic cat sprint?: A domestic cat can sprint up to around 48 km/h (30 mph) for short distances. They're ambush predators.
cats have 517 of these in their entire b: Cats have about 517 muscles, which give them flexibility and speed. Humans have around 650 muscles.
on what continent can aardvarks be found: Aardvarks live in sub-Saharan Africa. The name is Afrikaans for "earth pig".
how many young can an adult aardvark hav: An aardvark usually has a single young after a gestation of about seven months. The baby stays in the burrow at first.
what is the gestation period for an aard: The aardvark has a gestation period of about seven months. The newborn weighs about 2 kg.
what color was the aardvark from the pin: In The Ant and the Aardvark (1969), the aardvark is blue. It was part of The Pink Panther Show.
what is the gestation period of a dolphi: Dolphin gestation varies by species, from about 10 to 17 months. Bottlenose dolphins carry their young for about 12 months.
where in the world can you find the dolp: The boto (Amazon river dolphin) lives in the rivers of South America, including the Amazon and Orinoco. Adults are often pink.
which of these is not a part of the badg: Badgers are omnivores that eat earthworms, insects, small mammals, fruit and roots. Earthworms are a main food in Europe.
which of the following best defines the: An octopus's midden is a pile of shells and debris outside its den, from the animal's meals. Researchers use it to see what it eats.
octopuses have excellent vision. which o: Octopuses have excellent eyesight but are thought to be colorblind, with only one type of photoreceptor. They use polarized light and skin sensors.
what two continents did smilodon inhabit: Smilodon (saber-toothed cat) lived in North and South America, from the Pleistocene. Famous fossils come from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles.
approximately how long ago did smilodon: Smilodon went extinct about 10,000 years ago, at the end of the last Ice Age. The decline of large prey is one factor.
tomato frogs existence is threatened due: Tomato frogs are endangered because of habitat loss in Madagascar. They are red-orange and secrete a sticky substance.
due to the presence of a specific protei: Octopuses have blue blood because they use hemocyanin, a copper-based protein, to carry oxygen. Humans use iron-based hemoglobin, which looks red.
cockroaches are among the most resilient: Cockroaches can hold their breath for up to about 40 minutes, and they close their spiracles. They also survive weeks without food.
the flashlight fish, has a light-produci: Flashlight fish have organs below their eyes that host glowing bacteria. They can "blink" the light by covering it.
the giant panda and which of the followi: The giant panda and the dragon are both symbols of China. The dragon is a mythical symbol of power.
this animal is the second most expensive: Elephants are among the most expensive animals for zoos to keep after giant pandas, as they need space, food and care. An elephant can eat 150 kg of food daily.
when a panda is born, it is impossible t: Newborn pandas are tiny, about 100 g, which is a thousandth of their mother's weight. Sexing them can be hard at first.
how long does a panda usually live in ca: Giant pandas live about 20 years in the wild and up to 30 in captivity. The oldest known panda lived to 38.
in which country is the gohongaze starfi: Starfish are eaten in some Asian countries, where they are sold as snacks. In Japan, sea creatures are a big part of the cuisine.
what is located on the end of every arm: Starfish have an eyespot at the tip of each arm, which can detect light and dark. They have no brain.
what animal is the largest nocturnal pro: The aye-aye is the world's largest nocturnal primate (prosimian). It taps trees to find grubs with its long middle finger.
how deep can a bottlenose dolphin dive?: Bottlenose dolphins typically dive to about 300 m, and have been recorded much deeper. They can hold their breath for 8-10 minutes.
which continents does the natural habita: The jaguar's range stretches from Mexico through Central America to South America. It's the largest cat in the Americas.
which of the following statements is not: Jaguar cubs are raised only by their mother, and males provide no parental care. Cubs stay with her for up to two years.
what term is mainly used in literature t: A group of crows is called a murder. The term is folklore and appears in old English texts.
what do the beetles from the genus nicro: Burying beetles (Nicrophorus) bury small animal carcasses, and lay eggs on them for larvae to feed on. They care for their young.
what is the color of the eggs of all par: All parrot eggs are white. Many cavity-nesting birds lay white eggs as they don't need camouflage.
larger parrot species have longer life s: Large parrots such as macaws and cockatoos can live 60-80 years in captivity. Smaller parrots live 15-20 years.
what is the predominant color in amazon: Amazon parrots are mostly green. They have bright patches of color on the head and wings.
where does the female scorpion raise its: A female scorpion carries her newborn young on her back for the first weeks of life, until they molt. They then disperse.
what kind of substance does the female r: Female periodical cicadas lay eggs in slits in the twigs of woody plants. After hatching, nymphs drop to the ground and burrow.
what part of their body do the insects f: Jumping bristletails (Archaeognatha) spring into the air by flexing their abdomen. They are primitive wingless insects.
what is the main icon of the animal king: The Tree of Life is the centerpiece of Disney's Animal Kingdom in Florida, a 145-foot tree with carvings of 325 animals. It opened in 1998.
The giant anteater is about 2 m (6 ft) long, including its tail. It eats ants and termites.
this is a repulsive insect either black: Cockroaches can live for a week or more without their heads because they breathe through spiracles on their bodies. They die from lack of water.
this animal lives in africa. it has a re: Giraffes are very quiet, but they can hum at night. They eat leaves from acacia trees.
this animal is similar to a mouse but it: Rats breed quickly, with females having up to 5-6 litters a year. Each litter can have 6-12 pups.
these animals live in the sea. they are: Dolphins are mammals and breathe air through a blowhole. They sleep with half their brain at a time.
when this animal wants to defend itself,: A skunk sprays a foul-smelling liquid from glands near its tail. The smell can be detected from a long way away, up to a mile.
harry potter character sirius black was: In Harry Potter, Sirius Black is an Animagus who becomes a large black dog, nicknamed Padfoot. Peter Pettigrew becomes a rat and James Potter a stag.
what type of animal is the school superi: Webkinz is a line of plush toys, each with a code for an online virtual world. Characters include various animals in "Webkinz World".
what type of insect is the orange tip?: The orange tip (Anthocharis cardamines) is a European butterfly. Males have bright orange wing tips.
which insect would a myrmecophobic perso: Myrmecophobia is the fear of ants. The prefix comes from the Greek "myrmex", meaning ant.
a popular method of finding a vampires g: In vampire folklore, a virgin boy riding a white horse was said to find a vampire's grave. The horse would refuse to walk over it.
nabisco makes animal crackers in a plant: Nabisco makes Barnum's Animal Crackers, and one of its major bakeries is in New Jersey. The cracker box with a string handle dates to 1902.
chinese zodiac is not limited to just de: The Chinese zodiac assigns an animal sign for the year and an element (wood, fire, earth, metal, water). Together they form a 60-year cycle.
the slaughter of what animal is forbidde: Cow slaughter is banned in most Indian states, because cows are sacred in Hinduism. Laws differ by state.
what part of any animal is absolutely fo: Jewish dietary laws (kashrut) forbid eating blood. Meat is salted and soaked to remove it.
what is the common name for the rose spe: Rosa chinensis is called the China rose, or Bengal rose. It was key in breeding modern roses.
the name of what animal is missing in th: The proverb is "A tiger father has no dog sons", meaning a great parent will have great children. In Chinese, "虎父无犬子".
two fish swim into a concrete wall. one: The punch line is "Dam!" It's a pun, since a dam is a concrete wall, and "damn" is an exclamation.
the tiger is the national animal of whic: The tiger is the national animal of India, as well as Bangladesh, Malaysia and South Korea. India has about 70% of the world's wild tigers.
depending on the species, male deer are: Male deer are called bucks, stags or harts, and females are called does or hinds. "Does" are female.
what animal are the canary islands named: The Canary Islands are named after dogs, from the Latin "Insula Canaria", meaning "island of dogs". The canary bird was named after the islands.
the first mammal sent into space was thi: Laika, a Soviet dog, was the first animal to orbit Earth, aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957. She did not survive the mission.
humuhumu-nukunuku-a-pua'a is a word with: Humuhumunukunukuāpua'a is the reef triggerfish and Hawaii's state fish. The name means "triggerfish with a snout like a pig".
what animal has the broadest visual colo: Butterflies can see ultraviolet light, and some have many types of color receptors. Mantis shrimp have the most photoreceptor types.
prometea, an example of successfully clo: Prometea, born in 2003 in Italy, was the first cloned horse. She was a Haflinger.
what is the weight of the smallest known: The bee hummingbird's egg weighs about half a gram, and is the smallest bird egg. It's about the size of a pea.
what kind of animal is the primary host: Domestic cats and other felines are the definitive host of Toxoplasma gondii. Pregnant women are advised to avoid cleaning litter boxes.
what animal cell helped prove that membr: In 1970, Frye and Edidin fused mouse and human cells to show membrane proteins can move. It supported the fluid mosaic model.
you should expect this, if fish jump out: Fish often jump near the surface when insects are active, which may happen before rain. It's folk weather lore and not very reliable.
what is the average lifespan of a domest: Domestic rabbits live about 8-12 years with good care. Wild rabbits have shorter lives.
the now extinct species \"thylacine\" wa: The thylacine, or Tasmanian tiger, lived in Tasmania and mainland Australia. The last known one died in a zoo in 1936.
what is the scientific name of the commo: The scientific name of the common chimpanzee is Pan troglodytes. The bonobo is Pan paniscus.
what is the fastest animal?: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal, reaching over 320 km/h (200 mph) in a dive (stoop). The cheetah is the fastest on land.
what is the collective noun for bears?: A group of bears is called a sloth or sleuth. Bears are generally solitary.
\"decapods\" are an order of ten-footed: Decapods are crustaceans with ten legs, such as crabs, lobsters and shrimp. Krill belong to a separate order (Euphausiacea).
which of the following is true when alli: Alligators bellow, especially in the breeding season, to mark territory. Their bellow can make water dance on their backs.
which of these species is not extinct?: Komodo dragons are still alive (endangered), while the dodo, the Tasmanian tiger and the moa are extinct. Komodo dragons live on Indonesian islands.
what color/colour is a polar bear's skin: A polar bear's skin is black, which absorbs heat. Its fur looks white, but the hairs are clear and hollow.
what type of animal is a natterjack?: The natterjack is a toad found in Western Europe, with a yellow stripe down its back. It runs rather than hops.
what dog breed is one of the oldest bree: Pugs are one of the oldest dog breeds, dating back to around 400 BCE in China. They were pets of emperors.
what is the national bird of bahrain?: The white-eared bulbul is Bahrain's national bird. Bahrain's name for it is "bulbul".
three of these animals hibernate. which: Sloths don't hibernate, as they live in warm rainforests. Bears, bats and groundhogs do.
all of these animals are omnivorous exce: Snails are mostly herbivores, eating leaves, though some species eat meat. Omnivores include bears, pigs and humans.
these are typical australian animals exc: Sloths live in Central and South America, not Australia. Typical Australian animals include kangaroos, koalas and wombats.
representatives of three of these specie: Mosquitoes don't produce venom, but inject saliva that stops blood from clotting. Venomous animals include snakes, spiders and some lizards.
Penguins molt their feathers, but don't shed skin like snakes, lizards and frogs. They replace feathers every year.
the cobras most recognizable feature is: A cobra spreads its hood by stretching rib bones and loose skin to look bigger when threatened. It's a defensive display.
a baby cobra is fully able to defend its: A baby cobra is venomous from birth, and can defend itself within hours. Its venom is as potent as an adult's, but in smaller quantities.
which of these presidents had the most p: Theodore Roosevelt had a large menagerie at the White House, including a badger, snakes and a pony. His kids kept many pets.
what is the natural habitat of the snows: The snow leopard lives in the mountains of Central Asia, such as the Himalayas. It's endangered and has thick fur.
this freshwater mammal, found only in th: The baiji, or Yangtze River dolphin, was declared functionally extinct after a 2006 survey found none. It was a pale, nearly blind dolphin.
how many types of bats are there?: There are more than 1,400 bat species, making up about a fifth of all mammals. They are the only mammals that can fly.
which of the following is not a type of: True chipmunks include the least, yellow-pine and eastern chipmunk. "Bushy-tailed" describes some squirrels and woodrats.
which of the following is not a breed of: A ferret terrier is not a recognized dog breed. Real terrier breeds include Jack Russell and Airedale.
which of these is not a type of beetle?: Beetles are the largest order of insects, with 400,000 species. Examples include ladybugs, weevils and rhinoceros beetles.
one of these is not a true breed of chic: Real chicken breeds include the Rhode Island Red, Leghorn and Sussex. Many breeds are named for place names.
generally, how many times in an interval: Lions mate frequently, up to every 20-30 minutes over several days. A pair can mate 20-40 times a day.
cats twitch the tips of their tails slig: A slight tail twitch means focus or irritation, while a strong swishing or lashing tail shows displeasure or agitation. Context matters.
cats generally purr when they are happy,: Cats also purr when in pain, scared or ill, as a self-soothing mechanism. Purring vibrations may help healing.
how many different vocalization sounds d: Cats can make about 100 different sounds, whereas dogs make about 10. Many are used to communicate with humans.
pound for pound, humans are not the stro: The Hercules (rhinoceros) beetle can lift about 850 times its own weight. Ants and other beetles are also strong for their size.
human beings have 23 pairs of chromosome: Chromosome counts vary widely. Humans have 46, hermit crabs have over 250, and some butterflies have hundreds.
which of these animals has the largest p: The lynx has large, furry paws that act like snowshoes. This helps it walk on snow.
how long in years is the life span of an: Wild hippos live about 40-50 years. They spend most of the day in water.
this is the result of the gravitational: Tides result from the gravitational pull of the moon and, to a lesser degree, the sun on the oceans. Spring tides are strongest when they align.
this sea animal, widely considered the m: Oysters are valued for their meat and for pearls, produced by pearl oysters. They're found in shallow waters worldwide.
which of these mammals was brought to au: The dingo was brought to Australia by humans, about 3,500-4,000 years ago, probably by seafarers from Asia. It's a wild dog.
the diet of the koala consists mainly of: Koalas eat mostly eucalyptus leaves, which are toxic to most animals. They sleep up to 20 hours a day to save energy.
which lizard can squirt blood from the c: Horned lizards can shoot blood from their eyes, to deter predators like coyotes. They're sometimes called "horned toads".
the venomous lizard gila monster was nam: The Gila monster is named for the Gila River Basin in Arizona and New Mexico. It's one of the few venomous lizards.
geckos have immovable eyelids and cant b: Geckos lick their eyes, since they have no moveable eyelids, and have transparent scales covering the eye. Their long tongues are long enough.
this shark is considered a filter- feede: The whale shark filter feeds on plankton, krill and small fish. It's the largest fish.
which shark is the fastest swimmer?: The shortfin mako is the fastest shark, reaching up to about 74 km/h (46 mph). It can leap out of the water.
what is the common name for baby sharks?: Baby sharks are called pups. Some sharks lay eggs, while others give birth to live pups.
which of these is not a subspecies of gi: Giraffe subspecies (or species) include Masai, reticulated, Nubian, Rothschild's and Angolan. "East African giraffe" isn't a standard one.
the beagle was developed mainly for trac: Beagles were developed to track rabbits and hares, in packs. They have a keen sense of smell.
about how many years have beagles been a: Beagle-like dogs have existed for around 2,000 years, since the time of ancient Greece. The modern breed was developed in England in the 1800s.
which of the following cartoon dogs was: Snoopy, from Peanuts, is a beagle. He's Charlie Brown's pet.
the puggle is a mix between a beagle and: A puggle is a cross between a pug and a beagle. It's one of many "designer dogs".
this bird is the fastest animal on the p: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h (200 mph) in its hunting dive (stoop). It's the fastest animal.
which of these animals cannot be found i: The dingo lives in Australia and parts of Asia, and not in North America. Wolves, coyotes and bears are found in North America.
how many species of skunk exist?: There are around 11-12 species of skunk, in the Americas. They include striped, spotted and hog-nosed skunks.
how many young skunks can be born in one: A skunk litter usually has four to seven kits. Newborns are blind and deaf.
how many subspecies of red fox are found: India has three subspecies of the red fox, including the Indian desert fox. They are found in different regions.
which of the following is not a breed of: The Chinese Crested is a dog breed, not a chicken. Chicken breeds include the Silkie and the Orpington.
how many beats per minute does a chicken: A chicken's heart beats about 250-300 times per minute. Resting humans average 60-100.
a crocodile bite strength is up to how m: A saltwater crocodile's bite force can reach about 3,700 psi, among the highest of any animal. Humans bite at about 160 psi.
butterflies do not have lungs. they brea: Butterflies breathe through tiny holes called spiracles along the thorax and abdomen. These connect to tubes (tracheae).
how many hearts does a typical earthworm: Earthworms have five pairs of "hearts" (aortic arches), so 10 in total. They pump blood around the body.
how many species of earthworm are native: Australia has hundreds of native earthworm species, with about 650 described. Some are giant, such as the Gippsland earthworm.
how many fatal brown and grizzly bear at: Bear attacks on humans are rare but real. Staying alert, avoiding surprising a bear and carrying bear spray reduces risk.
which of these is only a dog food brand?: Cesar is a dog food brand, and a Mars Petcare product. Cesar Millan is a dog trainer.
what are cheetahs that have mutated patt: King cheetahs have blotchy stripes instead of spots, due to a recessive gene. They were thought to be a separate species.
in 2007 the amount of cheetahs left in t: Cheetah numbers have declined greatly, from about 100,000 a century ago to around 7,000 now. Estimates in 2007 were around 12,000.
what frog is the most poisonous?: The golden poison frog (a dart frog) of Colombia is the most poisonous frog. One frog can kill several people.
which of these types of frogs shares its: "Horned frog" shares a name with the "horned lizard" ("horned toad"), which is not a toad. Many common names mislead.
which one of these is not a species of z: The three true zebra species are the plains zebra, mountain zebra and Grévy's zebra. "Savanna zebra" is another name for the plains zebra.
which of these are not a function of a z: Zebra stripes may serve to deter biting flies, regulate temperature, confuse predators, and help recognition. They aren't warnings to other zebras.
the largest ant colony is located on the: The Ishikari supercolony in Hokkaido, Japan, has an estimated 300 million worker ants and a million queens. They are Formica yessensis.
what do we call the type of ants that pl: Harvester ants collect and store seeds as food. Leafcutter ants farm fungus.
The first ant fossil, found in New Jersey amber in 1966, was from the Cretaceous. It was named Sphecomyrma freyi.
which of these flamingo species is not n: The lesser flamingo lives in Africa and India. The American flamingo and Chilean flamingo live in the Americas.
why do flamingos often stand on one leg?: Flamingos stand on one leg, probably to conserve body heat. The exact reason is not settled.
when was the last reported killing of a: The last wild thylacine is thought to have been shot in 1930, in Tasmania. The last captive one died in 1936.
what was the fine for shooting a thylaci: Tasmania paid a bounty on thylacines, and only protected them in 1936, shortly before the last one died. Farmers blamed them for killing sheep.
although not all bear subspecies are vic: As humans take over habitats, bears come into contact with people more, causing more attacks. Food shortages also play a role.
surprisingly, the number one killer amon: Mosquitoes are the deadliest animals to humans, spreading malaria, dengue and other diseases. They cause hundreds of thousands to over a million deaths a year.
hyenas are most closely related to what: Hyenas are in the suborder Feliformia, closer to mongooses, civets and cats than to dogs. Many people think they're related to dogs.
how many species of moa are known to hav: Scientists recognize nine moa species, all extinct. The giant moa stood up to 3.6 m tall.
what was the main reason for the extinct: Moa were hunted to extinction by Māori settlers by around 1400, along with the loss of habitat. They were New Zealand's flightless giants.
in what year were the first moa remains: The first moa bone was brought to Richard Owen in 1839, who identified it as a giant bird. It was found in New Zealand.
approximately how many miles per year ca: Caribou make one of the longest land migrations, up to about 5,000 km (3,000 miles) a year. Herds travel in thousands.
which of these is not a species of reind: In North America, reindeer and caribou are the same species (Rangifer tarandus). "Northern caribou" is a common name for a population.
